chunks: 3805 - Ibn Muskan narrated from al-Halabi, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a group of people who bought cloth and all became partners in it, but did not divide it among themselves. Is it permissible for one of them to sell his share of the cloth before taking possession of it? He said: “There is no harm in it.”
And he said: “Indeed, this is not in the same category as food, because food is measured by volume.”

key_terms.بَزًّا: cloth or textile merchandise being bought and sold
key_terms.يَقْتَسِمُوهُ: they divide it among themselves into separate portions
key_terms.ٱشْتَرَكُوا: they jointly shared ownership in the purchased item
key_terms.ٱلطَّعَامِ: food, treated here under a distinct legal category

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell one’s share of jointly purchased cloth before taking possession of it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the sale of jointly owned cloth before physical possession. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام permits such a sale and distinguishes cloth from food, indicating that food has separate legal treatment because it is measured by volume.
